 Court No. - 72
 Hon'Ble Deepak Verma, J. 
1.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the record.

2. The present 482 Cr.P.C. application has been filed to quash the charge sheet dated 15.06.2020
and cognizance order dated 14.07.2020 as well as entire proceedings of Case No.4734 of 2020,
arising out of Case Crime No.08 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 Ipc and Section 3/4 of
D.P. Act, Police Station Mugalsarai, District Chandauli, pending before the Chief Judicial
Magistrate, Chandauli.
3.  Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that there is matrimonial dispute between the parties concerned.
The applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to ulterior motive.
It has further been submitted that the applicant resides in the neighbourhood of the husband of opposite party no.2 and has nothing to do with the matrimonial dispute between the parties.
Neither family members of the co-accused/in-law of the opposite party no.2 nor relative, no motive to demand of dowry from the opposite party no.2.

The opposite party no.2 with malice intention with ulterior motive has made accused as on perusal of the FIR, no offence under the aforesaid section is made out.
4.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. has vehemently opposed the submissions raised by learned counsel for the applicant but could not dispute the facts that the applicant is neighbour of co-accused.

5. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, as noted herein above, and also the submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, this Court is of the considered opinion that no useful purpose would be served by prolonging the proceedings of the above mentioned case.
The applicant is neighbour of the co-accused/in-laws having no involvement in demand of dowry.

In view of the Apex Court Judgement passed in the case of Geeta Mehrotra and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2012 (10) SCC 741, the Court has observed thus:-
" It would be relevant at this stage to take note of an apt observation of this Court recorded in the matter of G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693 wherein also in a matrimonial dispute, this Court had held that the High Court should have quashed the complaint arising out of a matrimonial dispute wherein all family members had been roped into the matrimonial litigation which was quashed and set aside.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra and Another Vs. State of Uttar Pradesh reported in 2012 (10) SCC 741
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: G.V. Rao vs. L.H.V. Prasad & Ors. reported in (2000) 3 SCC 693
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Their Lordships observed therein with which we entirely agree that:
?there has been an outburst of matrimonial dispute in recent times.
Marriage is a sacred ceremony, main purpose of which is to enable the young couple to settle down in life and live peacefully.

But little matrimonial skirmishes suddenly erupt which Ketan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189698459/
2 often assume serious proportions resulting in heinous crimes in which elders of the family are also involved with the result that those who could have counselled and brought about rapprochement are rendered helpless on their being arrayed as accused in the criminal case.

entities.text: Ketan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: There are many reasons which need not be mentioned here for not encouraging matrimonial litigation so that the parties may ponder over their defaults and terminate the disputes amicably by mutual agreement instead of fighting it out in a court of law where it takes years and years to conclude and in that process the parties lose their ?young? days in chasing their cases in different courts.?

The view taken by the judges in this matter was that the courts would not encourage such disputes."
6. In K.Subba Rao Vs. The State of Telangana (2018) 14 SCC 452, it was also observed that:-
" The Courts should be careful in proceeding against the distant relatives in crimes pertaining to matrimonial disputes and dowry deaths.

entities.text: K.Subba Rao Vs. The State of Telangana (2018) 14 SCC 452
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relatives of the husband should not be roped in on the basis of omnibus allegations unless specific instances of their involvement in the crime are made out."
7.

There are no materials on record to show that the ingredients required to constitute the offence alleged are discloses offence against the applicant to proceed towards trial, will be an abuse of process of law and is liable to be set aside.

8. Accordingly, the impugned charge sheet dated 15.06.2020 and cognizance order dated 14.07.2020 as well as entire proceedings of Case No.4734 of 2020, arising out of Case Crime No.08 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 of D.P. Act, Police Station Mugalsarai,
District Chandauli, pending before the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Chandauli, are hereby quashed.
9. This application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is accordingly allowed.

(Deepak Verma,J.) September 3, 2025 Mini  Ketan Singh vs State Of U.P. And Another on 3 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/189698459/
